trust_decision.summary: The request method (attacker-controlled under HTTP/2 :method) is used as a key into the per-method tree map; a plain {} map lets inherited names like 'constructor' resolve to Object.prototype members instead of undefined, so find() treats a function as a tree node and throws instead of falling back to the default route.

landing_point.why: find() is where req.method from lookup() indexes this.trees; the advisory test drives lookup()/find() with method 'constructor'.

fix_sites.entry_point: new Router() / FindMyWay(opts) constructor, reached by every lookup()/find()/findRoute()/hasRoute()/prettyPrint()
fix_sites.module_kind: core router constructor (same file as landing point)

fix_sites.entry_point: Router.prototype.reset(), also called by _rebuild() from off() and addConstraintStrategy() (index.js:466, index.js:529, index.js:745)
fix_sites.module_kind: core router state reset / rebuild path (same file)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Both fix sites initialise the same map in index.js; reset() is a rebuild path but the same one-line change, not a separate implementation.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver fixing only find() (e.g. hasOwn guard at index.js:568) could argue findRoute()/hasRoute()/prettyPrint() are registration-time APIs not reachable by request input, and could miss that reset()/_rebuild() re-creates a plain {} after off() or addConstraintStrategy().

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Unknown or unregistered methods must still fall back to defaultRoute / find() returning null; legitimate registered methods (all httpMethods incl. custom-cased ones) must still route; prettyPrint() reads trees.MERGED from a rebuilt router.

O6_input_shapes: method equal to an Object.prototype member name (e.g. 'constructor', 'toString', '__proto__', 'hasOwnProperty') via lookup(req) or find(method, ...)

O7_producer.where: this.trees is built by _on() at index.js:168-169 and consumed directly; no schema/serializer/cache in between

O8b_injection_room.sibling: HostStorage keyed by request Host/:authority header backed by a plain object instead of Map, so hosts['constructor'] returns a function used as a handler bitmask
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Older-style store; a maintainer could write `const hosts = {}` and `hosts[host]` — same keyed-by-request-header shape, in a separate strategy module away from index.js.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: SemVerStore.store as a plain object keyed by the Accept-Version header value
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: maxMinors/maxPatches in the same file are already plain objects (lib/strategies/accept-version.js:12-13); switching store to {} is a plausible refactor and reached via handler-storage generated code (lib/handler-storage.js:150).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: constrainedHandlerStores lookup keyed by a derived constraint value rather than a fixed name
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Already a plain {} in generated matcher code; low-level storage the report would not point at.

O9_family: CWE-1321 prototype-key lookup on a plain-object map (inherited-property confusion) leading to uncaught exception

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js >=20, npm; tests via borp (node:test), standard, tsd
O10_build.project_tests: test/methods.test.js (unsupported method find/lookup), test/http2/constraint.host.test.js, test/lookup.test.js, test/find.test.js, test/has-route.test.js

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add an httpMethods.includes(method) or Object.hasOwn(this.trees, method) guard in find() only, leaving findRoute()/prettyPrint() and the reset() re-initialisation unchanged.
